title: Jon Watts to Direct New Star Wars Trilogy Continuing Skywalker Saga
content:
Deadline reports that Lucasfilm has hired director Jon Watts to lead the first installment of a new trilogy intended to continue the Skywalker saga, with screenwriter Simon Kinberg attached to the project. Daisy Ridley is reportedly being considered to reprise her role as Rey, although the films have not yet been greenlit and few other details have been confirmed.

The article critiques the decision to return to the Skywalker family, describing the clan as having already shaped the galaxy through decades of cyclic conflicts involving Death Stars, Jedi orders, and dark side turnarounds. It suggests that while Star Wars has previously explored other corners of the galaxy through characters like smugglers and bounty hunters, the franchise has struggled to move away from the central family dynamic.

The piece notes that Watts, who directed Spider-Man: No Way Home, is seen as an inspired choice for the role, particularly given that his previous work centered on the concept of characters in long-running franchises not remaining dead. The author argues that relying on the same family saga is a waste of time, expressing a desire for newer worlds within the Star Wars universe.
summary: Deadline reports that Lucasfilm has hired Jon Watts to direct a new trilogy continuing the Skywalker saga, which is written by Simon Kinberg. Daisy Ridley is reportedly being considered to return as Rey, though the films have not yet been greenlit.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Bassam Tariq's Houston-set thriller stars Mahershala Ali as a Muslim hitman
content:
Mahershala Ali stars as Latif, a devout Muslim and contract killer, in the Houston-set thriller Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother, written and directed by Bassam Tariq. In the film, Latif fashions himself a righteous killer who justifies his violence as divine retribution against those he believes have offended God. According to Tariq, the character’s use of a sword is a central part of his code and a negotiation with his faith, with Tariq noting that using a sword forces one to strike with intention.

Tariq discussed the film in a recent interview in Toronto, where he reflected on his career pivot from a stalled reboot of Marvel’s Blade to this new project. The director stated, “I’m happier I made this movie,” indicating his satisfaction with the shift in focus to Ali’s thriller.
summary: Mahershala Ali stars as Latif, a devout Muslim who works as a contract killer in Bassam Tariq's Houston-set film. Tariq explains that the character's use of a sword is part of his code and a negotiation with his faith.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Seth Meyers mocks Trump's use of taxpayer funds for campaign ads
content:
Late-night hosts addressed Donald Trump’s use of taxpayer funds to finance campaign advertisements, a practice that has led Republican midterm candidates to distance themselves from the former president. The comedians focused on the unpopularity of Trump among these GOP candidates and his insistence that US taxpayers bear the cost of recycled campaign ads.

Seth Meyers specifically questioned the financial burden placed on the public, asking, “Is there anything this grub won’t make us pay for?”
summary: Late-night hosts discussed Donald Trump's use of taxpayer money to fund recycled campaign ads. They also addressed his unpopularity with GOP midterm candidates who are distancing themselves from him.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Dolly Parton sings Jolene in Welsh in posthumous recording
content: Dolly Parton’s niece Jada Star and Welsh singer Bronwen Lewis have announced that the country artist was proud to sing in Welsh. This statement accompanies the release of a recording in which Parton performs the song "Jolene" in the Welsh language.
summary: A recording of Dolly Parton singing Jolene in Welsh was released after her death. Her niece Jada Star and Welsh singer Bronwen Lewis stated that Parton was proud to sing in Welsh.
author: BBC Entertainment

title: K-pop giants Stray Kids join BTS in boycotting the Grammys
content: K-pop group Stray Kids have joined BTS in boycotting the Grammy Awards, becoming the second major act to withdraw from the ceremony. The decision by both groups is a response to the introduction of a new best Asian Pop award category.
summary: Stray Kids become the second major act to withdraw from the Grammys over the new best Asian Pop award.
author: BBC Entertainment

title: Alison Hammond has hospital heart check-up after leaving This Morning
content: Alison Hammond underwent a heart check-up in a hospital after departing midway through the broadcast of the television show This Morning on Friday. The host stated that she is currently "fine" but is undergoing the medical assessment following her early exit from the program.
summary: Alison Hammond is undergoing a heart check-up in the hospital after leaving midway through Friday's This Morning. The host stated that she is fine but is getting checked.
author: BBC Entertainment

title: Emmanuel Iyogun on his journey from reluctant prop to England debut
content:
Emmanuel Iyogun, the Northampton star and Spain-born son of Nigerian immigrants, earned his England debut off the bench in Argentina in July after a career defined by resilience. Head coach Steve Borthwick selected the prop for the match, marking a significant milestone in Iyogun’s unlikely journey to the international ranks.

Iyogun credits his parents’ advice for his determination, noting that he was always told he would have to work harder than others and might not receive initial privileges. This mindset led him to persist whenever he was told no or faced obstacles, viewing continued hard work as the only response. The article also highlights his recent interaction with Springbok forward Ox Nché, with whom he shared “massive cakes.”
summary: Emmanuel Iyogun, a Spain-born son of Nigerian immigrants, earned his England debut off the bench in Argentina in July. The Northampton star described his rise as requiring immense determination and resilience, noting that his parents always told him he would have to work harder than others.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Wakey-Wakey: Trinity’s rapid rise and Grand Final run shocks fans from long slumber
content:
Wakefield Trinity will face Warrington in their maiden Super League Grand Final on Saturday, an event expected to draw more than 70,000 supporters. The club’s rapid ascent stands in stark contrast to its status 965 days prior, when it played a match in Siddal, on the outskirts of Halifax, in front of only a few hundred spectators.

The transformation followed a takeover completed in late 2023 by boyhood Wakefield Trinity fan Matt Ellis, who has since injected £10m worth of investment into the organization. This financial commitment has led to visible results both on and off the field, propelling the club from a state described as a “shambles” to becoming a headline attraction in the sport.
summary: Club was a ‘shambles’ before takeover by boyhood Wakefield fan Matt Ellis – and on Saturday they face Warrington for the titleLast one out of Wakefield on Saturday, turn off the lights. Some 965 days ago, this story began on a field in Siddal on the outskirts of Halifax with just a few hundred people there to see it: this weekend, one of rugby league’s grand old clubs will be the headline attraction in front of more than 70,000 supporters when Trinity face Warrington in their maiden Super League Grand Final.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Prix de l’Arc de Triomphe: Waud seeks Hollywood ending after Snakes on a Plane
content:
Film producer George Waud, who spent 23 years in Los Angeles and recently served as a co-producer on the London West End revival of Cabaret, is the owner of Maltese Cross, the second favorite in the upcoming Prix de l’Arc de Triomphe. Waud acknowledged this week that he is not a typical owner for the most prestigious and valuable race of the European season, stating that he is making the most of the opportunity.

The horse’s journey to the Bois de Boulogne for the first Sunday in October includes a backstory rooted in Waud’s early life. Racing has been a consistent thread in his life since he took a trip to Newmarket with his mother in the 1970s. Maltese Cross will compete against runners from racing’s superpowers in the event.
summary: Film producer is certainly not a typical owner of the second favourite for the Prix de l’Arc de Triomphe with Maltese Cross part of a remarkable scriptAs George Waud is the first to concede, he is not a typical owner of the second favourite for the Prix de l’Arc de Triomphe. “No,” he said this week, three days out from the most prestigious and valuable race of the European season, when his colt Maltese Cross will take on runners from racing’s superpowers.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Mercedes team first as Russell and Antonelli face off at Sepang
content:
Mercedes has prioritized team strategy as title rivals George Russell and Andrea Kimi Antonelli prepare to face off during Formula One’s return to Malaysia. The event, officially designated as the “Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia,” marks the sport’s first visit to the Sepang circuit since 2017. Both drivers are bringing upgrades to the demanding track, which is known for its high temperatures and humidity that present a significant physical challenge.

The championship battle is further complicated by a resurgence from Red Bull, with Max Verstappen determined to make his mark on the title run-in. Despite the unusual naming convention that may puzzle statisticians, the focus remains on the competitive dynamics at the sharp end of the grid. The return to the much-liked Sepang circuit has been welcomed within the sport, setting the stage for a pivotal weekend in the season.
summary: Title rivals Russell and Antonelli bring upgrades to the first Grand Prix in Malaysia since 2017. The race is held at the demanding Sepang circuit, which is known for high temperatures and humidity.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Lib Dems urge Andy Burnham to reveal Manchester City owner meetings
content: Liberal Democrats have urged Manchester Mayor Andy Burnham to disclose details of all meetings held with Manchester City’s owners, the Abu Dhabi United Group (ADUG), and to declare any hospitality accepted at the Etihad Stadium. This call follows criticism of Prime Minister Rishi Sunak, who stated this week that he would be “really concerned” if ADUG were forced to sell the club after being found guilty of breaching Premier League financial regulations. The prime minister’s comments prompted Downing Street to issue two clarifications of his position on Thursday.
summary: The Liberal Democrats are calling for Andy Burnham to publish details of all meetings with Manchester City's owners and declare accepted hospitality. This follows criticism of the Prime Minister for expressing concern if the Abu Dhabi United Group were forced to sell the club.
author: Guardian Sport

title: If America wants to prosper, we must lead
content: Sen. Rick Scott and Hudson Institute Fellow Rebeccah Heinrichs argue that the United States must maintain its role as a global leader to counter an emerging authoritarian alliance led by China and Russia. They contend that American prosperity is directly tied to its ability to lead on the international stage.
summary: Sen. Rick Scott and Hudson Institute Fellow Rebeccah Heinrichs argue that the United States must maintain global leadership to counter an emerging authoritarian alliance led by China and Russia.

title: Hegseth orders US troops 1 day off to vote in October
content:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced on Friday that all U.S. troops will receive one day off in October to vote in the 2026 midterm elections. The stand-down order is scheduled to be executed on October 15.

Hegseth stated that this policy will continue in even-numbered election years as part of a new and “apolitical” Pentagon.
summary: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced that all U.S. Troops will receive one day off in October to vote in the 2026 midterm elections. The stand-down order is set for Oct. 15 and will continue in even-numbered election years.
author: The Hill

title: Trump motorcade neared 100 mph driving from Texas to Oklahoma due to storms
content: President Trump’s motorcade reached speeds approaching 100 mph on Thursday as the president drove from a rally in Texas to Oklahoma, opting for ground transportation after stormy weather in the South ruled out the use of a helicopter or airplane. The high-speed drive took place during the president’s travel from an event at the Peterbilt Motors manufacturing plant in Denton, Texas, to a second scheduled event in Durant, Oklahoma.
summary: President Trump drove from a rally in Denton, Texas, to Durant, Oklahoma, because stormy weather ruled out helicopter and airplane travel. His motorcade reached speeds near 100 mph during the journey.
author: The Hill

title: Tories prepare for election with focus on economy and welfare
content:
Kemi Badenoch has instructed her team to prepare for a possible early election as the Conservative Party aims to be election-ready ahead of its upcoming party conference. The leadership is emphasizing a strategic focus on key policy areas to position the party for potential immediate electoral challenges.

The party’s preparations will center on the economy and welfare, with Badenoch directing her team to prioritize these issues in their planning. This approach reflects an effort to ensure the Conservatives are fully prepared to campaign on these specific platforms should an early election be called.
summary: Kemi Badenoch has instructed her team to prepare for a possible early election. The party will prioritize the economy and welfare ahead of its conference.
author: BBC Politics

title: Big banks in net zero alliance continued lending to coal firms
content: New data indicates that global coal finance has remained steady since 2022, a trend observed as international efforts to reduce the connection between lending and emissions have waned. The findings highlight that major banks participating in the “net zero” alliance have continued to extend loans to coal companies.
summary: New data indicates that coal finance has remained steady globally since 2022. This trend occurred as international efforts to reduce the link between lending and emissions faded.

title: The Colorado River is shrinking. What happens next?
content:
Lake Mead, located in Nevada, has reached its lowest level since being filled nearly 90 years ago, while Lake Powell is also at a historic low. During a tour of the reservoir, Colby Pellegrino of the Southern Nevada Water Authority pointed out a large metal pipe protruding from a rock island, a feature that had previously been submerged.

Pellegrino identified the pipe as the first intake constructed in 1970 to deliver municipal water to the valley. The exposure of this infrastructure highlights the significant drop in water levels, which occurred during a visit when temperatures reached 42C (108F).
summary: Lake Mead is at its lowest level since it was filled nearly 90 years ago, Lake Powell also at a historic lowIt was 42C (108F) degrees as we motored across Nevada’s Lake Mead in our rented pontoon boat. Colby Pellegrino with the Southern Nevada Water Authority wanted to show us something we shouldn’t have been able to see.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Stem cell-derived brain models offer new window into anesthesia mechanisms
content: Hundreds of thousands of people undergo general anesthesia daily, relying on the procedure to safely induce unconsciousness during surgery. Despite decades of clinical use, the precise mechanisms by which anesthetic drugs alter the brain's electrical activity to produce this state remain incompletely understood by scientists.
summary: Scientists are using stem cell-derived brain models to investigate how anesthetic drugs reshape the brain's electrical activity to produce unconsciousness. This research aims to address the lack of understanding regarding how these drugs work, despite general anesthesia being used on hundreds of thousands of people daily.
author: Medical Xpress

title: UTSW study shows greater blood protein variability in MS patients using generic drugs
content:
A study led by researchers at the University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center (UTSW) indicates that generic versions of three commonly prescribed oral multiple sclerosis (MS) therapies may result in different biological outcomes compared to brand-name drugs. The research focused on patients taking these oral medications and measured blood proteins linked to MS disease activity.

The findings revealed that patients using the generic versions of the drugs exhibited greater variability in these blood protein markers than those taking the brand-name versions. This suggests that the generic formulations may produce less consistent effects on disease activity indicators in the bloodstream.
summary: UTSW researchers found that MS patients taking generic versions of three commonly prescribed oral therapies had greater variability in blood proteins associated with MS disease activity. Patients taking brand-name versions of those drugs had less variability in those proteins.
author: Medical Xpress

title: US pharmacy closures disproportionately affect racial minority communities
content:
Pharmacies across the United States are shutting down at a rapid pace, creating “pharmacy deserts” that leave millions of Americans without convenient access to essential health services. Research shows that nearly one in three pharmacies closed between 2010 and 2021, and more than 7,000 pharmacies have closed since 2019.

The surge in closures is disproportionately impacting racial minority communities, intensifying disparities in access to medication and health care. These communities now face heightened challenges in obtaining timely pharmacy services.

The continued loss of pharmacy locations threatens the health infrastructure of affected neighborhoods, underscoring the need for targeted interventions to address the growing gap in care.
summary: Pharmacies across the United States are closing rapidly, creating pharmacy deserts that leave millions without convenient access to care, and the closures are hitting racial minority communities the hardest. Research shows nearly one in three pharmacies closed between 2010 and 2021, including over 7,000 closures since 2019.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Lab-grown mini-bladder explains recurring urinary tract infections
content: Research into lab-grown "mini-bladders" is helping scientists understand why urinary tract infections (UTIs) frequently recur after initial treatment. For many individuals, the symptoms of a UTI, such as burning and frequent urination, disappear once antibiotics are finished but often return weeks or months later.
summary: Urinary tract infections often return weeks or months after antibiotics end. A lab-grown mini-bladder helps explain why these recurring infections happen.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Hidden lymphatic signal amplifier could inform treatments for lymphedema and cancer metastasis
content: Lymphatic vessels function as the body's drainage system by collecting excess fluid from tissues. When these vessels are underdeveloped, damaged, or dysfunctional, lymphatic drainage is impaired, leading to the development of lymphedema. This condition results in swelling that particularly affects the arms and legs.
summary: Lymphatic vessels function as the body's drainage system by collecting excess fluid from tissues. Impaired lymphatic drainage due to underdeveloped, damaged, or dysfunctional vessels can cause lymphedema, resulting in swelling in the arms and legs.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Ohio State study: Comparing past selves harms well-being
content:
A new study from The Ohio State University highlights that individuals often serve as their own harshest critics when evaluating their body image. The research indicates that people frequently compare their current selves to past versions, a process that can significantly impact their well-being.

This finding shifts focus from the traditional body image research, which has for decades concentrated almost exclusively on social comparisons and their toll on mental health. The Ohio State University study reveals that internal comparisons with one's own history are a critical factor in how individuals perceive their bodies.
summary: A new study from The Ohio State University indicates that comparing current selves with past versions is a major source of negative self-criticism. This finding contrasts with decades of body image research that focused primarily on social comparisons.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Ford retains No. 3 U.S. sales spot in Q3 despite 6.6% decline
content:
Ford reported a year-over-year sales decline of 6.6% during the third quarter, selling 507,395 light-duty vehicles. The automaker announced the figures on Friday.

Despite the drop in sales, Ford retained the No. 3 position in U.S. sales, fending off Hyundai.
summary: Ford reported a year-over-year sales decline of 6.6% during the third quarter. The company sold 507,395 light-duty vehicles while retaining the No. 3 U.S. sales position.
author: CNBC Business

title: G7 to release up to 100m barrels of emergency oil and diesel reserves
content:
Leaders of G7 nations have agreed to release up to 100 million barrels of emergency diesel and crude oil stockpiles in response to surging fuel prices. The decision follows pressure from Donald Trump to ease the impact of rising costs on households and economies.

The coordinated drawdown of reserves from some of the world’s largest economies will be managed by the International Energy Agency (IEA). According to French President Emmanuel Macron, the release of the oil and diesel is scheduled to take place within four months.
summary: G7 leaders agreed to release up to 100 million barrels of emergency diesel and crude oil stockpiles within four months. The coordinated drawdown, managed by the International Energy Agency, aims to ease surging fuel prices and pressure on economies.
author: Guardian Business

title: US adds 29,000 jobs in September as unemployment rises to 4.2%
content:
US employers added just 29,000 jobs in September, a sharp decline from previous monthly gains, while the unemployment rate rose slightly to 4.2%. This final jobs report before the midterm elections indicated a cooling labor market, with the figures falling to less than half of economists’ expectations for just under 70,000 new positions.

According to data from the US Bureau of Labor Statistics, most job gains were concentrated in the healthcare industry, which added 17,000 new jobs. Conversely, the information, financial, and professional industries experienced job losses during the period.
summary: US employers added 29,000 jobs in September, a figure under half of economists' expectations, while the unemployment rate rose slightly to 4.2%. Most job gains were concentrated in the healthcare industry, which added 17,000 new jobs, while the information, financial, and professional industries saw losses.
author: Guardian Business

title: Scotland Supermarkets Face New Rules on High Sugar, Fat, and Salt Products
content: New regulations in Scotland are set to restrict the placement of products high in sugar, fat, and salt within supermarkets. These measures aim to limit the visibility and accessibility of such items to consumers. Despite these changes to product placement, the meal deal remains available.
summary: Restrictions are being implemented in Scottish supermarkets to limit products with high sugar, fat, and salt content. Despite these new rules, the meal deal will continue to be available.
author: BBC Business

title: US Jobs Market Slows Ahead of Midterm Elections
content:
The U.S. jobs market experienced a sharp slowdown as American employers paused hiring activities. This shift in the labor landscape occurred with the midterm elections just one month away.

During this period, the unemployment rate rose slightly, reflecting the broader pause in new employment across the country.
summary: Unemployment rose slightly as American employers paused hiring. This slowdown occurred with midterm elections just a month away.
author: BBC Business

title: Multilingual readers report higher enjoyment and more daily reading, survey finds
content: The U.K.’s National Year of Reading is encouraging people across the country to “go all in” on reading. This initiative has prompted discussions among families regarding what to read, which language to use, and what form the reading should take.
summary: A survey found that multilingual readers report higher enjoyment of reading. The U. K.'s National Year of Reading encourages people to read more, but families are unsure what to read, in which language, and in what form.
author: Phys.org

title: New research shows how water would behave on the moon
content:
New research shows how water would behave on the moon.

As humanity looks toward future bases on the moon, plant cultivation will be critical for sustaining life there.

Plants can provide food, oxygen, medicine, water purification and waste recycling, making them indispensable for lunar development.
summary: Humanity looks toward future bases on the moon, and plant cultivation will be critical for sustaining life there. Plants can provide food, oxygen, medicine, water purification and waste recycling, making them indispensable for lunar development.
author: Phys.org

title: Red squirrels endangered in Britain as range shrinks, says expert
content:
Red squirrels, once common across Britain, have largely vanished from much of their former range.  

Dr. Kat Hamill, senior lecturer in zoology at Nottingham Trent University, explains the factors behind the decline of this native mammal and discusses whether scientific research and conservation efforts can help restore its population.
summary: The red squirrel, once a familiar sight across Britain, has disappeared from much of its former range. Dr. Kat Hamill, senior lecturer in zoology at Nottingham Trent University, explains the causes and whether science and conservation can help restore the species.
author: Phys.org

title: CHARA Array Finds Infrared Edge Darkening Gaps in Stellar Models
content:
Astronomers using Georgia State University's Center for High Angular Resolution Astronomy (CHARA) Array have discovered that nearby stars darken more strongly toward their edges at near‑infrared wavelengths than current stellar atmosphere models predict.

The study shows that the limb‑darkening effect is stronger in the near‑infrared than the widely used models anticipate, exposing gaps in the theoretical description of how stars distribute their light.

These observations provide a new benchmark for understanding the structure of stars and the accuracy of existing stellar atmosphere models.
summary: Astronomers using Georgia State University's Center for High Angular Resolution Astronomy (CHARA) Array found that nearby stars darken toward their edges more strongly at near-infrared wavelengths than predicted by several widely used models of stellar atmospheres. This finding provides a new benchmark for understanding how stars are structured.
author: Phys.org

title: KIT researchers develop enzyme beads for greener chemical production
content:
Researchers at the Karlsruhe Institute of Technology (KIT) have created a method to assemble enzymes into millimeter‑sized beads that can be stored and used as biocatalysts. In the new technology, the enzymes serve both as the catalytic agents and as the structural material of the beads.

A variant of the approach allows the enzyme networks within the beads to be combined with living cells, expanding potential applications. The team has filed a patent application for the technology, and the findings were published in the journal Advanced Materials.
summary: Researchers at the Karlsruhe Institute of Technology have developed a method to assemble enzymes into millimeter‑sized, storable beads that act as both catalyst and structural material. A variant combines the enzyme networks with living cells, a patent application has been filed, and the work was published in Advanced Materials.
author: Phys.org

title: Patriot Front White Nationalists March in Washington on July 4
content:
In the lead-up to the nation's 250th birthday on July 4, images of a large demonstration in Washington circulated on television and social media. Hundreds of masked men marched through the streets carrying flags and chanting "Reclaim America!"

The marchers were identified as members of Patriot Front, a white nationalist group, based on logos displayed on their identical baseball caps.
summary: Hundreds of masked men marched through Washington carrying flags and chanting “Reclaim America!” The marchers were identified as members of Patriot Front, a white nationalist group.
author: Phys.org

title: Study Finds First Week of Life Crucial for Future Allergy and Eczema Risk
content: A recent study involving hundreds of infants challenges the prevailing scientific consensus that the immune system develops without distinct critical phases. The research indicates that the first week of an infant's life is a crucial period that significantly influences future health outcomes, specifically regarding the risk of developing allergies and eczema.
summary: The mainstream view holds that there are no critical phases in immune system development. A study of hundreds of infants indicates that the first week of life may be crucial for future allergy and eczema risk.
author: New Scientist

title: Mathematicians and AI in behind-the-scenes battle over truth in math solutions
content:
AI models are solving mathematics problems at an increasing pace, with a technique known as formalisation serving as the key method for demonstrating the correctness of their claimed solutions. This process has sparked a behind-the-scenes battle among mathematicians and AI systems regarding the nature of mathematical truth.

The central question facing the field is whether the formalisation process itself can be trusted to accurately verify these AI-generated solutions.
summary: AI models are solving mathematics problems at an increasing pace. A formalisation technique is key to proving the correctness of their claimed solutions, but its reliability is in question.
author: New Scientist

title: Fossil mammal with reptile-like teeth shows lifelong tooth replacement
content:
An ancient mammal species from the Cretaceous period, discovered in China, challenges existing understanding of mammalian evolution due to its unique dental capabilities. Unlike most modern mammals, which develop only two sets of teeth during their lifetime, this fossil species appears to have possessed the ability to replace its teeth continuously throughout its life.

The discovery highlights a significant deviation from standard mammalian traits, as the animal retained a reptile-like characteristic in its dentition. This finding provides new insights into the evolutionary history of mammals, suggesting that the transition to a two-set dental system occurred later than previously thought for some lineages.
summary: An ancient Cretaceous species found in China can replace its teeth throughout its life. This lifelong tooth replacement differs from most modern mammals, which only get two sets of teeth.
author: New Scientist

title: NASA Opens Applications for Next Class of Flight Directors
content:
NASA has opened applications for the next class of flight directors, a highly respected role in human spaceflight. The position will be based in mission control at NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston, Texas.  

Flight directors are essential to NASA’s mission of advancing American leadership in space exploration, particularly as the agency works toward a sustained human presence on the Moon. The role involves leading teams that manage spacecraft operations and mission-critical decisions.  

Applicants can apply now for the upcoming class of flight directors.
summary: NASA is seeking leaders for the flight director position in mission control at its Johnson Space Center in Houston, a role critical to advancing American leadership in space exploration and paving the way for a sustained human presence on the Moon. Applications are being accepted for the next class of flight directors.
author: NASA News

title: NASA Langley Conducts First Unsteady Pressure Sensitive Paint Tests in Transonic Dynamics Tunnel
content:
Researchers at NASA’s Langley Research Center in Hampton, Virginia, conducted groundbreaking tests to develop new wind tunnel capabilities for future aircraft design. The experiments took place in the center’s Transonic Dynamics Tunnel, marking a significant step in advancing aerodynamic research.

In a first-of-its-kind test, the research team utilized unsteady Pressure Sensitive Paint to analyze how air flows around a standard wind tunnel model. This innovative approach allows for detailed observation of aerodynamic forces during testing.
summary: Researchers at NASA’s Langley Research Center in Hampton, Virginia, used unsteady Pressure Sensitive Paint to study air flow around a standard wind tunnel model. This first-of-its-kind test in the Transonic Dynamics Tunnel is paving the way for new wind tunnel capabilities for designing future aircraft technologies.
author: NASA News

title: NASA abre solicitudes para próxima promoción de directores de vuelo
content:
La NASA ha abierto las solicitudes para la próxima promoción de directores de vuelo, un puesto considerado uno de los más prestigiosos en el ámbito de los vuelos espaciales tripulados. Estos profesionales se desempeñarán en el control de misión del Centro Espacial Johnson, ubicado en Houston.

La agencia destaca que esta función es fundamental para reforzar el liderazgo dentro de sus operaciones espaciales.
summary: La NASA busca líderes para el puesto de director de vuelo en el control de misión del Centro Espacial Johnson de Houston. Esta función es fundamental para reforzar el liderazgo en el ámbito de los vuelos espaciales tripulados.

title: Redditor Buys Used CPU, Finds It Was Banned on Valorant, Now SoL
content: A Redditor purchased a used central processing unit (CPU) that was subsequently discovered to be banned on the game Valorant. The incident was shared in a post on the r/LinusTechTips subreddit, where the user described being stuck with the non-functional hardware. title: GRPO Credit Assignment Fixed Without Step-by-Step Evaluation
content:
A new research paper titled "Fixing GRPO's credit assignment problem without evaluating every step" has been posted on arXiv. The work addresses a specific challenge within the Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) framework, focusing on improving credit assignment mechanisms without the computational cost of evaluating every individual step.

The paper is currently available at arXiv identifier 2609.36178. It has been shared on the Hacker News platform, where it has received 11 points and no comments to date.
summary: The paper proposes a solution to the credit assignment problem in GRPO. It does so without evaluating every step.

title: Power Approval Set to Delay Oracle's Wisconsin AI Datacenter
content:
Power approval set to delay Oracle's Wisconsin AI datacenter

A recent article reports that the approval of power for Oracle’s planned AI datacenter in Wisconsin has been delayed. The delay is expected to postpone the project’s timeline, although no further details about the cause or projected new dates are provided in the source.

The article can be accessed at https://www.theregister.com/on-prem/2026/10/02/power-approval-set-to-delay-oracles-wisconsin-ai-datacenter/5300832. Discussion of the story appears on the Hacker News link https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49934569, where it has received 21 points and 4 comments.
summary: Oracle's Wisconsin AI datacenter will be delayed by a power approval. The approval is set to cause the delay.
author: Hacker News

title: America.gov Launches with 20-Year Cookie, Raises Tracking Concerns
content:
America.gov launches with privacy pledge amid tracking concerns

A new article on Biometric Update reports that the U.S. government’s website, America.gov, has launched with a privacy pledge. The launch has raised questions about tracking, as the code for the site’s login system, Login.gov, is under scrutiny for potential data collection practices.

The story was shared on the tech discussion platform Hacker News, where it received 30 points and sparked 9 comments from users. The article’s URL is https://www.biometricupdate.com/202610/america-gov-launches-with-privacy-pledge-as-login-gov-code-raises-tracking-questions.
summary: America.gov has launched with a privacy pledge. The launch includes a 20-year-long permanent cookie and has raised tracking questions.
author: Hacker News

title: New Biological De-Aging Contest Starts, LLMs Lack Reasoning
content:
The Download, a weekday technology newsletter, announced a new contest that pits competitors against each other in a race to biological youth. The competition, described as “unusual,” rewards participants for achievements that are not detailed in the brief announcement.  

Jessica Hamzelou, the newsletter’s contributor, revealed that she has officially signed up for the contest. The article does not provide further details about the contest’s structure, prizes, or eligibility requirements.
summary: A new contest pits competitors against each other in a race to biological youth. Jessica Hamzelou signed up for the competition this week, and the article notes that LLMs do not reason.
author: MIT Tech Review

title: Enterprise AI Moves to Full Operational Flight as Global Investment Hits $2.5 Trillion
content:
Enterprise AI is no longer a future ambition; it is in full operational flight. Model capabilities are advancing faster than most organizations can absorb, while the cost of performance continues to fall.

Globally, AI investment is set to reach $2.5 trillion in 2026, up 44% from the previous year. For many enterprises, this investment has…
summary: Enterprise AI has moved from a future ambition to full operational flight, with model capabilities accelerating faster than most organizations can absorb and performance costs falling. Global AI investment is projected to reach $2.5 trillion in 2026, up 44% from the previous year.
author: MIT Tech Review

title: Fi Mini and Tractive Cat Trackers Compared: Trade-Offs Highlighted in 2026 Review
content:
In a recent review of smart cat trackers, the author compared the Fi Mini and Tractive models. The evaluation focused on the devices’ performance over several months of monitoring a cat named Basil, tracking both activity and sleep patterns.

After months of monitoring Basil’s activity and sleep, the author found that Fi and Tractive cat trackers come with their own trade‑offs.
summary: The author monitored Basil’s activity and sleep for several months using Fi and Tractive cat trackers. The review notes that each tracker has its own trade-offs.
author: Wired

title: Amazon stops using NDAs with county officials for data center projects
content:
Amazon announced that it will no longer use nondisclosure agreements, described as secret agreements, with county officials for its data‑center projects. The change comes as the company acknowledges growing community opposition.

Amazon said the backlash has contributed to the emergence of data‑center moratoriums in various locations across the United States.
summary: Amazon announced it has ended the use of NDAs with county officials for its data centers. The company said community backlash is prompting data center moratoriums across the country.
author: Wired

title: Trump’s AI Rebrand Tested Tech Exec Loyalty—and It Worked
content: Billionaires who had previously expressed intense enthusiasm for artificial intelligence complied with Donald Trump’s decision to cancel the term, effectively passing a loyalty test for tech executives. These industry leaders shifted their public stance to align with the president’s rebranding efforts, despite their prior obsession with the technology.
summary: Billionaires had promoted AI for years, yet they complied when Trump cancelled the term. The rebrand tested their loyalty and succeeded.
author: Wired

title: Trillium Labs Plans to Publicly Showcase Self-Improvement Research
content: Trillium Labs intends to conduct high-stakes research on self-improvement and model behavior in a transparent manner, contrasting with many frontier labs that keep similar risky research locked away. The organization aims to publicly showcase its work in these specific areas.
summary: Many frontier labs keep their risky research locked away. Trillium Labs wants to show off its work on self-improvement and model behavior.
author: Wired

title: Home Assistant Renames Cloud Service to Home Assistant Link, Drops Cloud from Logo
content:
Home Assistant, an open-source smart home platform, is renaming its cloud service to Home Assistant Link and removing the cloud from its logo. Founder Paulus Schoutsen told The Verge, “We are renaming Home Assistant Cloud to Home Assistant Link, because we hate clouds,” adding, “Big tech ruined the cloud, so we're out.”

The rebranding is part of a long-term strategy by Schoutsen and his team to establish Home Assistant as a mainstream smart home platform. Schoutsen noted that most users discover the powerful platform after reaching the limits of mainstream options such as Google Home, Amazon Alexa, and Apple Home. He acknowledged that the platform has a steep learning curve.
summary: Home Assistant is renaming its cloud service to Home Assistant Link and removing the cloud from its logo. Founder Paulus Schoutsen said the change reflects the company's dislike of cloud services, citing that big tech ruined the cloud.
author: The Verge

title: Tesla Q3 production rises 3.8% but sales fall year-over-year
content:
Tesla reported that it produced a total of 464,391 vehicles during the third quarter of this year, marking a 3.8 percent increase compared to the same period in 2025. The production figures included 457,387 Model 3 and Model Y units, along with 7,004 "other vehicles" such as the Cybertruck, Cybercab, and Tesla Semi. The company noted that it had discontinued the Model S and X earlier this year.

Although Tesla sold fewer vehicles in the third quarter than it did a year ago, when consumers rushed to utilize expiring federal tax credits for electric vehicle purchases, the company still exceeded Wall Street estimates. These results suggest that Tesla’s recovery remains on track despite the year-over-year sales decline.
summary: Tesla produced 464,391 vehicles in the third quarter, a 3.8 percent increase from the same period in 2025. The company sold fewer vehicles than a year ago when consumers used expiring federal tax credits, but still beat Wall Street estimates.
author: The Verge

title: Paramount’s Warner Bros. megamerger will just be called Skydance
content:
Paramount Skydance CEO David Ellison announced that the company will be rebranded as Skydance upon the completion of its $110 billion merger with Warner Bros. Discovery next week. In a post on X, Ellison stated that the new name was chosen to provide the combined entity with its own identity while keeping the Paramount and Warner Bros. brands in the spotlight.

The merger is set to close after a judge earlier this week approved a settlement between Paramount and California, along with 11 other states that had sued over the planned acquisition. This legal resolution cleared the final major hurdle blocking the deal.
summary: Paramount Skydance CEO David Ellison announced the merged company will be called Skydance when it completes its $110 billion merger with Warner Bros. Discovery next week. A judge approved the settlement Paramount reached with California and 11 other states that sued over the acquisition, clearing the last major hurdle blocking the deal.
author: The Verge

title: Keurig Launches Alta Machine with Plastic‑Free, Compostable Coffee Pucks
content:
Keurig has introduced the Keurig Alta, a new single-serve coffee machine designed to eliminate the use of plastic and aluminum recyclable pods. The company first unveiled the machine and its companion AltaRounds two years ago. These puck-shaped replacements wrap pressed coffee grounds in a plant-based coating derived from seaweed.

The AltaRounds are described as 100 percent compostable. Although they are currently packaged in plastic wrappers to maintain freshness, Keurig is working to transition to paper wrappers, according to CNET.

The Keurig Alta is now available for preorder at a price of $499.99.
summary: Keurig’s new Keurig Alta single‑serve coffee machine uses AltaRounds, puck‑shaped pods made from a seaweed‑derived, plant‑based coating that is 100 percent compostable. The pods currently come in plastic wrappers but the company plans to switch to paper, and the Alta is available for preorder at $499.99.
author: The Verge

title: Tesla adds mid‑charge drive feature after Idaho Supercharger shooting
content:
Tesla has introduced a software update allowing drivers to disengage their vehicles from charging stations in an emergency. This new feature addresses a safety concern that emerged following a mass shooting at a Supercharger location in Twin Falls, Idaho, in August, which resulted in four deaths and seven injuries.

Previously, Tesla vehicles locked the charging plug into the port and disabled the drive function while connected to a charger. To move the car, owners had to manually release the cable from the charging port. Following the Idaho incident, Tesla owners called for a quick-release mechanism to facilitate a faster escape during emergencies.

This week, Tesla responded to those requests by rolling out the software update that enables drivers to drive off mid-charge if necessary.
summary: Tesla released a software update that lets drivers drive off while charging in emergencies. The update was prompted by a mass shooting at a Supercharger in Twin Falls, Idaho that left four dead and seven wounded.
author: The Verge

title: OpenAI launches Dots, a $100/month business-focused assistant
content:
OpenAI has launched Dots, a new agentic assistant that the Verge describes as resembling its competitor, Muse, but tailored for professional use. The service is positioned as a business-first product with a minimum monthly cost of $100. While Dots allows users to create characters similar to those in Muse, its early marketing emphasizes capabilities for completing business tasks, such as launching websites, rescheduling calls, and building slide decks for board meetings.

In contrast, the article notes that Muse focuses more on personal interactions, such as reminding users to purchase items they have viewed. The Vergecast recently discussed Dots and the current state of agentic assistants, highlighting the differing approaches of these two platforms.
summary: OpenAI released Dots this week, a business-first assistant costing a minimum of $100 per month. The product is marketed for tasks such as launching websites, rescheduling calls, and building slide decks for board meetings, contrasting with Muse's personal reminder focus.
author: The Verge

title: Nacon Revolution 5 Unlimited PS5 controller features built-in screen and audio mixing
content:
Nacon has announced the Revolution 5 Unlimited, which the company claims is the first officially licensed PlayStation 5 controller featuring a built-in screen. This display allows users to adjust settings, such as joystick sensitivity and button remapping, directly on the gamepad.

The controller’s screen also supports audio mixing from multiple sources. When headphones are connected via a cable, users can simultaneously listen to music from a phone and audio from a PS5 game.

The Revolution 5 Unlimited is currently available for preorder for $229.99 through Nacon’s online store, with shipments expected later this year.
summary: Nacon announced the Revolution 5 Unlimited, which it claims is the first officially licensed PS5 controller with a built-in screen for adjusting settings. The device allows users to mix audio from their phone and console when using wired headphones and is available for preorder at $229.99.
author: The Verge

title: Last Chance: Apply for Side Event at TechCrunch Founder Summit 2026
content:
Less than 24 hours to apply for a Side Event at Founder Summit 2026

The deadline to submit a proposal to host a Side Event at TechCrunch Founder Summit 2026 is rapidly approaching. Organizers report that applicants have less than 24 hours left, with the final application window closing tonight at midnight PT.

The Founder Summit will take place in Boston from November 1–7. Hosting a Side Event offers participants the chance to engage directly with the local startup ecosystem, bring their community together, and launch conversations that could shape the future of the region.
summary: Applications for hosting a Side Event at TechCrunch Founder Summit 2026 close tonight at midnight PT. The Summit runs from November 1–7 in Boston, inviting participants to connect with the local startup ecosystem.
author: TechCrunch

title: Last 24 Hours to Book Exhibit Table at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026
content:
TechCrunch Disrupt 2026: Final Day to Secure Exhibit Space

Today marks the last day to book an exhibit table for TechCrunch Disrupt 2026. The event will run from October 13–15 at San Francisco’s Moscone West, drawing more than 10,000 founders, investors, operators, and tech leaders. Participants will be on the lookout for companies, products, ideas, and people worth knowing.  

The question for exhibitors remains: will they find your startup?
summary: Today is the last day to book your exhibit table at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026. From October 13–15, 10,000+ founders, investors, operators, and tech leaders will arrive at San Francisco’s Moscone West looking for companies, products, ideas, and people worth knowing.
author: TechCrunch

title: Clay CEO Kareem Amin discusses rise of GTM engineer at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026
content:
Clay Co‑founder and CEO Kareem Amin will speak at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026. He will join the AI Stage to discuss the rise of the GTM engineer.

Attendees can register for a ticket and receive a second pass at 50 % off.
summary: Clay Co-founder and CEO Kareem Amin will speak on the rise of the GTM engineer at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026. Attendees can register for a ticket and receive a second pass at 50% off.
author: TechCrunch

title: Jas Khaira of Blackstone to Speak on Next‑Gen AI at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 Builders Stage
content:
Blackstone executive Jas Khaira is scheduled to speak on the Builders Stage at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026, where he will discuss building next‑generation artificial intelligence.

The event offers a promotion: attendees can register for a pass and receive 50 % off a second pass.
summary: Jas Khaira of Blackstone will take the Builders Stage at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 to discuss building next‑gen AI. Registrants can receive a 50% discount on a second pass.
author: TechCrunch

title: Laytr launches app that saves any online content, not just articles
content:
Laytr has launched a new app that expands the range of online content users can store for later use. Unlike tools that focus solely on articles, the app allows users to save articles, recipes, screenshots, videos, PDFs and other items.

The service keeps saved material private and synchronizes the archive across Apple devices, ensuring access wherever users go.
summary: Laytr's new app lets users save articles, recipes, screenshots, videos, PDFs and more for later. The archive remains private and syncs across Apple devices.
author: TechCrunch

title: Pope Leo XIV Criticizes AI-Generated Art
content:
Pope Leo XIV has publicly criticized AI-generated art, stating that it differs fundamentally from human-created works. In a recent statement, he wrote that there is an ontological difference, even before an aesthetic one, between art and what a machine can generate through statistical calculation based on millions of images created by others.

The pope added that algorithms lack the spark of humanity, underscoring his view that machine-produced images cannot replicate the essence of human artistic creation.
summary: Pope Leo XIV says there is an ontological difference between art and what a machine can generate through statistical calculation based on millions of images created by others. He argues that algorithms lack the spark of humanity.
author: TechCrunch

title: Australia Orders Legacy Tech Review After OpenAI Medicare Breach
content:
The Australian government is confronting significant “tech debt” after the OpenAI Medicare breach, a cyber‑attack that exposed vulnerabilities in legacy systems and could lead to a large bill for taxpayers.  

In response, the Home Affairs Department has ordered all federal agencies to conduct a “legacy technology stocktake.” Each agency must develop a plan to reduce legacy technology systems to a level that fits within its risk tolerance and appetite.  

The review is part of a broader effort to fortify defenses against future AI‑agent attacks, and the order was issued this week.
summary: The Australian government has ordered a review of legacy technology after the OpenAI Medicare breach. Agencies must plan to reduce legacy systems to meet risk tolerance, potentially costing taxpayers a large bill.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Brown bear slams into car in Hokkaido, police release dashcam footage
content:
A video released by police shows a brown bear slamming its body against a car in northern Japan. The incident occurred after two bears were spotted on a road in Hokkaido.

The larger bear, believed to be the mother, approached the vehicle before running away with its cub. The driver was unharmed, and police have made dash‑cam footage of the encounter publicly available.
summary: A brown bear slammed its body against a car in northern Japan after two bears were spotted on a road in Hokkaido. The driver was unharmed, the larger bear (believed to be the mother) ran away with its cub, and police released dashcam footage of the encounter.
author: Euronews

title: US sends third carrier strike group to Middle East in biggest buildup since 2003
content:
The United States has dispatched a third carrier strike group to the Middle East, marking the largest buildup in the region since 2003. The move underscores a significant increase in U.S. military presence in the area.

The USS Theodore Roosevelt departed San Diego on Sunday, accompanied by a Marine expeditionary unit of more than 2,000 troops. This deployment brings the potential total U.S. military presence in the region to over 60,000 personnel.
summary: The USS Theodore Roosevelt left San Diego on Sunday. It was accompanied by a Marine expeditionary unit of more than 2,000 troops, bringing the potential total US military presence in the region to more than 60,000.
author: Euronews

title: Mobile lab in Butembo, DRC provides Ebola test results within 24 hours
content: A mobile laboratory in Butembo, eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, is shortening the time it takes to diagnose Ebola. The facility now delivers test results within 24 hours of sample collection and, on occasion, as quickly as six hours. This rapid turnaround improves patient care and helps contain the spread of the disease.
summary: A mobile laboratory in Butembo, eastern DRC, is accelerating Ebola testing. Results are now available within 24 hours and sometimes as quickly as six.
author: Euronews

title: 5,000 drones create shapes over Nanchang for China's National Day
content:
A fleet of 5,000 drones illuminated the night sky over Nanchang, creating a giant light show as China marked National Day.  

The coordinated display formed shapes that included fighter jets, robots, planes and horses, producing a spectacular visual performance.  

The event was part of the National Day celebrations in the city.
summary: A fleet of 5,000 drones formed fighter jets, robots, planes and horses over Nanchang. The display was part of China's National Day night show.
author: Euronews

title: DR Congo Ebola outbreak kills more than 4,000, officials report
content:
The Democratic Republic of Congo’s Ebola outbreak, described as the worst ever in the country, has killed more than 4,000 people, according to official figures released on Friday. The death toll comes from a total of more than 8,000 confirmed cases.

Congolese officials reported the numbers on Friday, highlighting the severe impact of the epidemic across the nation.
summary: The worst ever Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has killed more than 4,000 people. Congolese officials said on Friday that the outbreak has produced over 8,000 confirmed cases.
author: Euronews

title: U2 mark 50-year anniversary with low‑key surprise gigs in Dublin
content:
U2 marked their 50‑year milestone with a series of surprise, low‑key concerts in Dublin, the band’s hometown.  

Although the group could have filled stadiums for the golden anniversary, they opted to return to their roots and celebrate with intimate gigs in the city where they began.  

The surprise shows underscore the band’s decision to honor half a century of music on a modest, local scale.
summary: U2 are celebrating 50 years as a band. They opted for a few low‑key surprise concerts in their hometown of Dublin instead of large stadium shows.
author: France 24

title: Cornell 7 allegations ignite fury over gang rape culture at Ivy League university
content:
Allegations of a gang rape at an American Ivy League university have ignited a firestorm on social media, prompting widespread criticism of how colleges and universities manage sexual assault cases. The controversy, highlighted under the banner “The Cornell 7,” has drawn intense public scrutiny of campus policies and response mechanisms.

In France, the parliament is debating a major new bill intended to combat violence against women and children. Annette Young interviewed Dr Andreea Gruev‑Vintila, a social psychologist who helped draft the legislation, to discuss its scope and potential impact.

Separately, the king of Morocco announced the appointment of Marrakesh mayor Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri as the country’s first female prime minister.
summary: Allegations of a gang rape at an American Ivy League university have set social media alight, sparking widespread fury over how colleges handle sexual assault cases. The French parliament is debating a new bill to combat violence against women and children, and Morocco’s king has named Marrakesh mayor Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri as the country’s first female prime minister.
author: France 24

title: Thousands of Indian women protest after suspected gang rape of 17-year-old in New Delhi
content:
Thousands of women across India have taken to the streets demanding stronger protection for female students after a suspected gang rape of a 17‑year‑old girl in an upscale neighbourhood of New Delhi. The protests, described as a mass movement, call for safer public spaces rather than restrictions on women’s access to them.

In response to the incident, authorities in New Delhi increased protective measures, though demonstrators argue that limiting women’s presence in public areas does not address the root of the problem. The protests underscore a broader demand for improved safety and gender‑based violence prevention nationwide.
summary: Thousands of women have taken to the streets across India demanding better protection for female students after a suspected gang rape of a 17‑year‑old girl in an upscale neighbourhood of New Delhi. Authorities have beefed up protective measures, but the protesters say limiting women's access to public spaces is not the answer.
author: France 24

title: 45-year-old Senator Flavio Bolsonaro ties with President Lula in Brazil election polls
content:
Flavio Bolsonaro, a 45‑year‑old Brazilian senator, has emerged as a presidential candidate who was still relatively unknown in Brazil just a few months ago.  

Recent polling shows Bolsonaro neck and neck with incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva as the country heads toward the upcoming presidential election.  

Analysts note that a Bolsonaro victory would place Brazil among a growing list of Latin American nations that have shifted to the right or far right in recent months.
summary: He was still relatively unknown in Brazil a few months ago. The 45-year-old senator is now neck and neck with incumbent President Lula in the polls for the upcoming presidential election.
author: France 24

title: EU states urged to plan gas and electricity savings as fuel prices surge
content:
EU member states have been urged to prepare gas and electricity savings as a harsh winter approaches, amid sharply rising fuel prices across the bloc.  The average price of diesel has climbed to well above €2 per litre, up from roughly €1.50 in October of last year, prompting alarm over the cost‑of‑living impact on households.

The surge in energy costs comes as the conflict in the Middle East adds further pressure, leaving Europeans with limited relief before winter.  EU governments have introduced measures aimed at cushioning ordinary people from the rising prices, and a review is underway to assess the effectiveness of those actions.
summary: EU member states are being urged to prepare gas and electricity savings as diesel prices rise above €2 per litre, up from about €1.50 in October. The article reviews measures to cushion ordinary people from higher energy costs amid a harsh winter and ongoing Middle East conflict.
author: France 24

title: Brazilian voters line up Sunday as merch sales surge for Lula and Flavio Bolsonaro
content:
Nearly 159 million Brazilians are set to vote in general elections on Sunday, choosing new members of parliament, reshaping two‑thirds of the Senate and selecting the country’s next president.  

While the ballot remains secret, supporters are displaying allegiance openly, with flags for candidates and parties lining the streets of Rio de Janeiro. Vendors report a surge in sales of merchandise for incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and his rival Flavio Bolsonaro.  

The report on the merchandising frenzy was filed by France 24’s Brazil correspondent Jan Onoszko.
summary: Nearly 159 million Brazilians will vote in general elections on Sunday, choosing MPs, Senate seats and the president. Vendors in Rio de Janeiro report booming sales of merchandise for President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and rival Flavio Bolsonaro as supporters display flags and apparel.
author: France 24

title: EU Parliament foreign affairs chair McAllister calls for urgent defence gap closure
content:
EU Parliament Foreign Affairs Committee chair David McAllister warned that the European Union must urgently close defence gaps to address growing security threats. In a recent interview, McAllister said the bloc “is not at war with the Russian Federation, but we are no longer at peace with Russia,” underscoring heightened tensions with Moscow.

He added that the EU is still unable to make sovereign decisions in certain defence areas because it remains “too dependent on US capabilities.” The committee chief called for swift action to reduce this reliance and strengthen Europe’s own security posture.
summary: David McAllister, chair of the European Parliament’s Foreign Affairs Committee, said the EU must urgently close defence gaps. He said the EU is not at war with the Russian Federation but is no longer at peace with Russia, and that dependence on US capabilities prevents the EU from making sovereign defence decisions.
author: France 24

title: Lula, 80, runs for fourth term, neck‑and‑neck with Flavio Bolsonaro
content:
President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva will stand for re‑election in Brazil on Sunday, seeking a fourth term in office. The 80‑year‑old former steelworker is positioning his campaign around his personal popularity and the country’s recent economic successes.

Lula’s bid places him in a close contest with far‑right rival Flavio Bolsonaro, with both candidates neck‑and‑neck in the latest polls. The race is shaping up as a direct showdown between the incumbent president and Bolsonaro’s challenger.
summary: President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, an 80‑year‑old former steelworker, will stand for re‑election on Sunday, seeking a fourth term. He is neck‑and‑neck in the polls with far‑right rival Flavio Bolsonaro.
author: France 24

title: Turkey stock market scandal hits half a million investors
content:
A stock‑market scandal in Turkey is reported to have affected about half a million investors. Authorities say asset managers artificially inflated the value of their funds, prompting investigations.

Turkish officials have carried out multiple arrests linked to the scheme, and a leading lawmaker from the ruling AKP party has resigned in its wake.
summary: Asset managers are alleged to have artificially inflated the value of their funds, sparking a scandal that has affected half a million investors. Turkish authorities have made multiple arrests and a leading AKP lawmaker has resigned.
author: DW World

title: Expedition to Kiribati's Nikumaroro island targets lagoon anomaly in Earhart case
content:
Nearly 90 years after US aviator Amelia Earhart vanished over the Pacific, a new expedition has been launched to the remote Kiribati island of Nikumaroro.  

The team hopes that an anomaly observed in a lagoon on the island could finally reveal the fate of Earhart’s missing aircraft.  

The expedition marks the latest effort to solve the long‑standing mystery surrounding Earhart’s disappearance.
summary: Nearly 90 years after US aviator Amelia Earhart vanished over the Pacific, a new expedition has been launched to the remote island of Nikumaroro. The team hopes a lagoon anomaly on the island could finally reveal the fate of her missing aircraft.
author: DW World

title: Argentina launches cash-for-citizenship scheme with $350k gift or $800k bond
content:
Argentina has launched a cash‑for‑citizenship scheme aimed at investors seeking the fastest, though most expensive, path to Argentine citizenship.  

Under the new program, applicants may either make a non‑refundable gift of $350,000 or purchase a government bond for $800,000, depending on their preference and financial strategy.
summary: Argentina has introduced a cash-for-citizenship program that offers the fastest path to Argentine nationality. Investors can obtain citizenship by making a non‑refundable gift of $350,000 or by purchasing a government bond for $800,000.
author: DW World

title: Iran accused of blocking SIM cards and online accounts to silence dissent
content:
DW reports that several Iranians say the government has blocked their SIM cards, bank access and online accounts. According to the interviewees, the restrictions were lifted only after they deleted critical content or pledged to cease activism.

The accounts of the individuals suggest a systematic use of digital controls to silence dissent, with access to essential services contingent on compliance with the demands. No further details were provided.
summary: DW reported that several Iranians said their SIM cards, bank access and online accounts were blocked. The blocks were lifted only after they deleted critical content or pledged to stop activism.
author: DW World

title: Spain's parliament rejects housing bill amid protests over pensioner eviction
content: Spain’s minority government suffered a defeat in parliament after it attempted to push through a pair of emergency measures aimed at making housing more affordable. The measures were introduced in response to a pensioner’s eviction and the protests that followed. The parliamentary vote rejected the bill, halting the government's effort to address the housing affordability crisis.
summary: Spain's minority government was defeated in parliament when its emergency housing measures were rejected. The bid was prompted by a pensioner's eviction and ongoing protests.
author: DW World

title: WHO urges massive aid influx into Gaza ahead of winter amid delayed medicines
content:
The UN World Health Organization (WHO) called on Friday for a massive influx of aid into Gaza before winter, warning that repeated delays in delivering lifesaving medicines, prosthetics and other essential supplies from Israel could have devastating consequences for Palestinians in the war‑torn enclave.

The WHO said the ongoing holdups jeopardize urgent health needs, emphasizing that the lack of timely deliveries threatens the well‑being of residents who depend on these critical resources.
summary: The UN World Health Organization said on Friday that repeated delays in bringing lifesaving medicines, prosthetics and other supplies from Israel into Gaza could have devastating consequences for Palestinians. It appealed for a massive influx of aid before winter.
author: UN News

title: Escalating fighting in Yemen worsens food security crisis, WFP warns
content:
The World Food Programme (WFP) warned on Friday that renewed conflict in Yemen has triggered a surge in hunger, deepening the country’s food security crisis.  

The WFP said the increased hunger could have consequences in the wider region and beyond.  

The agency’s warning underscores the potential regional impact of Yemen’s escalating fighting.
summary: Renewed conflict in Yemen has triggered a surge in hunger. The World Food Programme warned on Friday that the hunger could have consequences in the wider region and beyond.
author: UN News

title: UN rights chief Volker Türk says Haiti gang violence is adapting and expanding
content:
Haitians remain trapped in a cycle of lethal gang violence, according to the United Nations’ top human‑rights official.  

Volker Türk said on Friday that gang violence in Haiti continues to “adapt and expand,” keeping the country in a state of ongoing danger for its residents.
summary: Haitians remain in the grip of lethal gang violence. The UN’s top rights official Volker Türk said on Friday that the violence is adapting and expanding.
author: UN News

title: US Coast Guard intercepts cargo ship Grace carrying fuel to Cuba on Sept. 5
content:
The U.S. Coast Guard announced that it intercepted a large cargo ship carrying fuel bound for Cuba, as the Trump‑era oil embargo on the island remains in effect.  

The vessel, named Grace, was boarded on 5 September in the Caribbean Sea between Cuba and Mexico.  Coast Guard officials said the ship was using tactics to evade authorities and was thought to be part of a common “dark fleet” operation.  The New York Times reported the ship was 91 metres (300 ft) long.  

After boarding, the Grace was taken to Mexico.
summary: The US Coast Guard said it boarded the cargo ship Grace, which was carrying fuel bound for Cuba, and stopped it on 5 September in the Caribbean Sea between Cuba and Mexico. The vessel was using dark fleet tactics to evade authorities and was taken to Mexico as the Trump administration’s oil embargo against Cuba continued.
author: Guardian World

title: India youth ‘cockroach’ protests target Modi’s election chief
content:
India’s youth‑led “cockroach” movement has returned to the streets, directing its protests toward a senior bureaucrat identified as Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s prized election chief.  

The demonstrators are focusing on the official who oversees what is described as the world’s biggest elections, seeking to challenge his role ahead of upcoming polls.
summary: India’s youth protests, referred to as the “cockroach” movement, have returned to the streets. The protests are aimed at Prime Minister Modi’s prized bureaucrat who oversees the world’s biggest elections.
author: Al Jazeera

title: G7 to release 100 million barrels in four months, Trump praises Europe diesel deal
content:
Paris – French President Emmanuel Macron announced that the Group of Seven will release 100 million barrels of oil from strategic reserves over the next four months, with the diesel portion of the release “front‑loaded.”  

In the United States, President Donald Trump praised a separate Europe diesel deal, describing it as a significant achievement.

title: Golden Boy returns to London stage after 40 years with Josh O'Connor
content:
Boxing continues to draw large audiences despite a decline in the sport’s general popularity, largely due to its enduring appeal in storytelling. This connection is highlighted by the London revival of Lillian Hellman’s 1937 play, Golden Boy, which had not been performed in the UK in over 40 years. The drama centers on a young violinist in Depression-era America who abandons his musical talent to pursue fame and wealth in the boxing ring.

The current production features Josh O’Connor in the lead role, a performer known for his film Knives Out and the series Wake Up Dead Man. O’Connor’s portrayal is noted for its physical authenticity, including powerful attacks on a heavy bag that raise concerns for his hands and visible abdominal definition that is not solely the result of makeup. The play’s premise, which blends the disciplines of music and combat, serves as a focal point for examining why boxing remains a box-office success.
summary: The 1937 play Golden Boy, about a violinist who becomes a boxer, is being performed in London for the first time in over 40 years. Josh O'Connor stars in the production, bringing his acting skills to the role of a gifted young man lured into boxing.

content:

Beyond diagnosis, the test enables physicians to evaluate how a patient’s cancer responds to treatment. It also helps predict whether immunotherapy or chemotherapy is likely to be the most effective therapeutic option for each individual patient.

content:

The study, which also appeared in The Lancet Regional Health Americas journal, focused on patients under the age of 45 who developed the condition. The EASD conference took place from September 28 to October 2.
summary: New research presented at the EASD Annual Meeting in Milan shows that low-energy diets combined with structured exercise can reverse early-onset type 2 diabetes in about half of participants.
