title: Study links >90‑day spaceflights to higher astronaut hip fracture rates
content:
A study published in Mayo Clinic Proceedings reports that astronauts experience a higher rate of hip fractures after spaceflights lasting more than 90 days compared with those who undertake shorter missions or with individuals who are not astronauts.  

The research highlights the need for expanded assessment of astronauts’ long‑term skeletal health following extended periods in space.
summary: New research found that astronauts have higher rates of hip fractures after spaceflights lasting more than 90 days compared with shorter flights or non‑astronauts. content:

content:

Farmer Sander Roeleveld operates a small white combine harvester to plow his crops and harvest the grain, which has never before been harvested in the Netherlands. The harvest marks the first time rice has been gathered in the country.
summary: In a soggy field between Amsterdam and The Hague, farmer Sander Roeleveld used a small white combine harvester to harvest rice, a grain never before harvested in the Netherlands. The harvest is part of a Dutch test of a new crop intended to help sinking peatlands.

content:
Switzerland’s glaciers have shed almost one‑fifth of their mass over the past five years, according to experts speaking on Thursday. The rapid loss, described as “catastrophic,” reflects the glaciers’ heightened vulnerability to climate change.

The melt recorded in 2026 was the second‑largest on file, underscoring the accelerating pace of ice loss across the Swiss alpine region.

title: Swiss glaciers lose nearly 20% of ice over five years, 5.5% shrink in early 2026
content:
Switzerland has lost almost one‑fifth of its glacier ice over the past five years, according to new research, marking a dramatic reshaping of the Alpine landscape. Scientists say the country’s large white glaciers have been reduced to “moon‑like rock deserts” as melt rates accelerate.

An annual monitoring report shows Swiss glaciers shrank by 5.5 % in the first eight months of 2026, following a summer of scorching heatwaves and a winter with little snow. The recent loss brings the total reduction of glacier ice since 2021 to 19.4 %, just shy of the record set in 2022.

The rapid melt is linked to the heat‑trapping effects of fossil‑fuel pollution, which is causing extreme glacier collapse across Alpine regions in Europe.
summary: Research shows Switzerland has lost almost one‑fifth of its glacier ice over the past five years. Swiss glaciers shrank by 5.5% in the first eight months of 2026, bringing total loss since 2021 to 19.4%, just below the 2022 record.

title: Yantra LALR(1) parser generator for C++ builds full AST before walking
content:
Show HN: Yantra – an LALR(1) parser generator for C++  

Yantra, posted on Hacker News, is a C++ parser generator that produces a lexer, parser and abstract‑syntax‑tree (AST) walker from a single tool. Unlike most LALR parser generators such as Yacc, Bison or Lemon, which execute semantic actions during bottom‑up parsing, Yantra first builds the complete AST and then walks it top‑down in a separate pass. This design lets a parent rule’s action run before its children are visited and enables a single grammar to define multiple walkers—for example, one that emits C++ and another that emits Java—from the same parse.

The tool includes an integrated lexer with mode support (e.g., for nested comments) and offers an optional amalgamated single‑file output mode that generates a main() function. Yantra targets C++23, is released under the MIT license, and is currently at version 0.5.1 (pre‑1.0) with a single maintainer. Known gaps are listed at https://github. Com/TantrixAuto/yantra/blob/main/docs/known_l..., and the repository is hosted at https://github. Com/TantrixAuto/yantra. Feedback and questions are welcomed; the author will be monitoring comments.

The Hacker News post has earned 23 points and generated 14 comments.
summary: Yantra is a C++ parser generator that produces a lexer, parser, and AST walker from a single tool and constructs the entire AST before a separate top‑down walk. It includes an integrated lexer with mode support, optional single‑file output, C++23 compatibility, MIT licensing, and can generate multiple walkers such as C++ or Java emitters.

title: Vivo X Fold 6’s size and aspect ratio feel dated ahead of global launch
content:
Vivo’s X Fold 6, which debuted in China in June, is now being prepared for a global launch. The device retains the dimensions of Vivo’s earlier foldables and mirrors the size of many pre‑Apple and pre‑Samsung models that used a more square‑ish form factor.

Its 6.51‑inch cover screen follows a standard 20:9 smartphone aspect ratio, while the unfolded panel expands to an 8.02‑inch display that is nearly square. Reviewers note that the crease remains more visible than on competing devices, and the phone carries an IP59 rating for water and dust resistance.
summary: Vivo's X Fold 6 launched in China in June and is now ready for a global release. title: Australian communications minister Anika Wells named Time’s most influential rising star
content:
Australian federal communications minister Anika Wells has been included on Time magazine’s “world’s most influential rising stars” list. The recognition highlights her role in implementing Australia’s under‑16 social‑media ban and confronting major technology firms.

Wells’ efforts helped bring the country’s restrictions on children’s use of social media into force last year. The measures have drawn international attention, with several European and Asian governments, as well as some U.S. states, adopting or considering comparable policies.

Time’s listing cites Wells’ work on the ban and her challenges to big‑tech companies as the basis for her selection.
summary: Anika Wells, Australia’s federal communications minister, was named one of Time magazine’s “world’s most influential rising stars”. The honor recognizes her work on the country’s under‑16 social media ban and her efforts to challenge big‑tech companies.

content: Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey warned that the rapid expansion of artificial‑intelligence investments could lead to market shocks. He said the central bank is monitoring the “waves of cash being invested in artificial intelligence” very carefully. Bailey’s remarks highlight the regulator’s heightened scrutiny of the AI boom’s potential impact on financial stability.
summary: Andrew Bailey said the AI boom could trigger market shocks. He said the Bank of England is watching the waves of cash being invested in artificial intelligence very carefully.

title: US-led coalition ends 12-year anti-ISIS mission in Iraq
content:
The US‑led coalition announced the end of its anti‑Islamic State mission in Iraq, citing heightened regional tensions and security concerns.  

The force had been operating in Iraq for 12 years, working to dismantle ISIS networks that had threatened to take over the region and plunge it into instability.  

The decision marks the conclusion of a long‑running effort to counter the militant group’s influence in Iraq.
summary: The US-led coalition announced the end of its anti‑Islamic State mission in Iraq. The force had operated in Iraq for 12 years to dismantle ISIS networks that had threatened to take over the region and plunge it into instability, amid heightened regional tensions and security fears.

content:

content:
Japan’s conservative leader Sanae Takaichi announced new, tightened measures for foreigners seeking permanent residency in Japan.  

The announcement follows Takaichi’s historic supermajority election victory in February, during which she pledged extensive immigration reforms. The new residency measures are presented as part of her effort to fulfill those election promises.

title: Most lost body fat is exhaled as CO2, study finds
content:
When body fat is reduced, most of it does not simply disappear as solid waste. Researchers have quantified the fate of lost fat, finding that about 84 % of it is expelled from the body as carbon dioxide through exhalation, while the remaining 16 % is eliminated as water.

These figures clarify that the primary route for fat loss is through the respiratory system, with a smaller portion leaving the body in liquid form.
summary: Researchers estimate that around 84% of lost body fat is exhaled as carbon dioxide. The remaining 16% is lost as water.

title: Death row inmate Christa Pike hospitalized after surviving two lethal injections
content:
US death row inmate Christa Pike is in a hospital after, according to her lawyers, she survived two lethal injections.  

Pike was 18 when she and her boyfriend beat and killed 19‑year‑old Colleen Slemmer at a job‑training camp for young people.  

The hospitalization follows the failed execution attempts, but no further details were provided.
summary: Christa Pike, a US death row inmate, is in hospital after surviving two lethal injections, according to her lawyers. Pike was 18 when she and her boyfriend beat and killed 19‑year‑old Colleen Slemmer at a job training camp for young people.

title: Swiss Glaciers Lose 5.5% of Ice in Second-Biggest Melt on Record
content:
Swiss scientists report that Swiss glaciers have lost 5.5 % of their ice, marking the country’s second‑largest melt on record.  

The rapid ice loss is most pronounced at the Rhône Glacier, where heatwaves and a dry winter have accelerated the retreat.  

The melt event is the second‑biggest in Switzerland’s history, driven by the combination of high temperatures and low precipitation.
summary: Swiss scientists report rapid ice loss at the Rhône Glacier, with glaciers losing 5.5% of ice in Switzerland’s second-biggest melt on record. Heatwaves and a dry winter are driving the loss.

title: Flydubai flight to Israel avoids disaster after pilot stabbed, attacker unknown
content:
A flydubai flight bound for Israel was attacked, resulting in the pilot being stabbed.  The attacker’s identity and motive remain unknown.

Saudi and UAE authorities have confirmed that investigations are underway but have provided little public information beyond that.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu reported that the copilot was arrested.

title: Over 600 detained and dozens of police injured in French school protests
content:
Hundreds of students were detained and dozens of police officers injured during violent school protests in France, authorities reported. More than 600 people, most of them students, have been taken into custody amid the escalating unrest.

The protests began last week when secondary‑school students mobilised to protest a shortage of teachers, overcrowded classrooms and what they described as unreasonable timetables. The demonstrations have turned increasingly violent, leading to the injuries of police officers and the detentions of a large number of participants.
summary: More than 600 people, most of them students, have been detained and dozens of police officers injured amid increasingly violent school protests in France. The protests began last week when secondary school students started mobilising against a shortage of teachers, over-crowded classrooms and what they argued were unreasonable timetables.

title: Russia launches heaviest attack on Ukraine's energy grid in months
content:
Russia carried out its heaviest combined assault on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure in months on Wednesday, targeting the power grid and heating facilities. The strikes killed seven people and forced emergency power cuts in Kyiv and surrounding regions.

Officials warned that the attacks come as Ukraine faces a difficult winter, with Russian forces intensifying assaults on the country’s power and heating systems. The emergency outages were triggered in response to the damage inflicted by the combined assault.
summary: Russia launched its heaviest combined assault on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure in months on Wednesday, killing seven people and triggering emergency power cuts in Kyiv and nearby regions. title: El Salvador Sets 2027 Election Date, Bukele Eyes Third Term
content:
El Salvador’s electoral tribunal announced that the next presidential election will be held on February 28, 2027. The decision was made on Wednesday, setting the official date for the vote.

The new election timetable opens the possibility for President Nayib Bukele to run for a third term, following constitutional amendments that removed presidential term limits. Bukele’s bid for a third term is now possible under the revised legal framework.

Bukele has been praised for sharply reducing gang violence in the country, but his crackdown has also drawn criticism for alleged rights abuses.
summary: El Salvador will hold presidential elections on February 28, 2027, allowing President Nayib Bukele to run for a third term after term limits were removed. Bukele has been praised for sharply reducing gang violence but criticized for rights abuses during his crackdown.

content:

The airline and authorities are monitoring the situation closely. Follow the liveblog for further updates.

content:

The Portuguese Football Federation president, Pedro Proença, travelled to Copenhagen to try to ease the situation, but was unable to resolve the conflict. Ronaldo’s exit means he must now explain his decision.
summary: Cristiano Ronaldo left Portugal’s training camp in Denmark after several days of tensions with head coach Jorge Jesus. content:

The decision was issued over the dissent of the three liberal justices on the court.
summary: The Supreme Court on Wednesday ruled that Tennessee can put Christa Pike to death, lifting an eleventh-hour appeals court ruling that had paused the execution. The court’s decision clears the way for the state’s first execution of a woman in more than 200 years.
